title: Red and near-infrared light
summary: Natural dusk red/NIR and optional panels—evening spectrum for wind-down, not a substitute for outdoor light timing.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Red and near-infrared (NIR) light sit at the long-wavelength end of the solar band people discuss for evening wind-down and recovery. Twilight and sunset naturally carry more red/NIR relative to midday blue sky. Therapeutic red/NIR panels are optional gear that overlap that spectrum conversation—they are not a substitute for outdoor light timing.

sections.heading: Why it shows up in the Light pillar
sections.body: Evening outdoor light is warmer and lower intensity than noon. Lifestyle communities treat that band as friendlier for skin and wind-down than mid-day UV burn risk. Photobiomodulation research studies red/NIR devices for tissue recovery in clinical and sports settings with mixed, dose-dependent results. This app’s habit starts with free dusk outdoors; panels are optional when you already own them.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Prefer natural dusk outdoors when weather allows—same window as sunset viewing. If you use a red/NIR panel, follow the device’s distance and time guidance; do not stare into high-intensity LEDs. Log duration in 15-minute blocks or custom minutes. Keep evening blue hygiene after you come indoors so a panel session is not followed by a cold white laptop for hours.

sections.heading: What is solid vs framework
sections.body: Solid ground: sunset and twilight are redder than noon sky; some red/NIR device studies show local tissue effects at specific doses. Framework / teaching layer: that any home panel recreates solar dusk biology, or that red light alone fixes circadian timing without morning outdoor light and true dark sleep. Panels are tools; solar timing is still the spine of the Light pillar.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Log Red / near-IR light for natural dusk exposure or a panel session with duration. Pair with Sunset viewing and Evening blue-light hygiene: outdoor solar signal first, then dim artificial light indoors. Educational only—not a medical phototherapy prescription.
